platforms.description:
At the ninth hour (Psalm 22:1, Matthew 27:46), Jesus cried out into the dark: "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"

Raw anguish, yes. But also a quotation. Those exact words were written down, in the first person, almost a thousand years earlier, by a king who died old and safe in his own bed.

This film walks the whole song: the death David never died, the wounds written early, the honest question of how a poet saw Golgotha ten centuries out, the turn in the middle of the psalm, and its last line, which lands on the same note as the cross's last word: he hath done this. It is finished.

A reverent deep-dive through Psalm 22 with every quotation verbatim KJV.

He was forsaken so that you never will be. Come and see where the song was pointing.

platforms.description:
At the ninth hour (Psalm 22:1), nailed to a Roman cross, Jesus gathered his strength and cried out: "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" (Matthew 27:46).

We hear raw anguish, and it is that. But it is also a quotation. Those exact words had been written down, in the first person, almost a thousand years before that morning, by a king who died old and safe in his own bed:

"My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?" (Psalm 22:1, KJV).

This deep-dive walks the whole song in seven movements:
1. The Cry - the quotation inside the anguish
2. A Death David Never Died - the first-person scandal
3. The Wounds Written Early - pierced hands and feet, the parted garments, the lots
4. The Honest Question - how could a poet see Golgotha ten centuries out?
5. He Quoted the Whole Song - what reaching for the first line means
6. The Turn - the psalm does not end in the dark (Hebrews 2:12)
7. He Hath Done This - the last line and the cross's last word, on the same note

Every quotation verbatim KJV. Reverent documentary pace, inked graphic-novel visuals.

He was forsaken so that you never will be. However far you have run, the way home is open, and he opened it from the dark.
